open_points.subject: resubmission of an implementation with an existing verdict for the unchanged corpus
open_points.text: “recorded once and then reused, never computed again” contradicts “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again while the corpus digest is unchanged, does admission create new TrialExecution records, or does it return the recorded verdict without running the cases?
options: Reuse the recorded verdict and create no new TrialExecutions
Run every active case again and create new TrialExecutions, while still retaining the original verdict
open_points.default_guess: Reuse the recorded verdict and create no new TrialExecutions.

witness.initial: Implementation I already has an admitted verdict for corpus digest C.
events: An agent submits content equal to I again while the corpus is still C.
outcomes: The kernel reuses the verdict, performs no sandbox executions, and creates no TrialExecution records.
The kernel runs every case again and records new TrialExecutions, but activation still uses the previously recorded verdict.
witness.observer: The submitting agent inspecting trial evidence and the slot's recent records.

open_points.subject: function purity and admissible implementation behavior
open_points.text: The product calls a function “pure” and says “no clock, no randomness,” while the changed K-02 says code obtaining time or chance another way “is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.”
open_points.question: Is independence from time and chance a required fact of every function implementation, or is it only enforced by blocking the standard-library entry points while other time- or chance-dependent code remains eligible for trial and admission?
options: All time- or chance-dependent implementations are invalid because functions are pure
Only the named standard-library entry points are blocked; other time- or chance-dependent implementations can be admitted when their observed outputs pass
open_points.default_guess: Only the standard-library entry points are blocked, and other dependencies are judged by observed outputs.

witness.initial: A submitted implementation obtains a chance-dependent bit without calling the standard library's blocked randomness entry points.
events: An authoring agent submits the implementation.
outcomes: The implementation is refused because a function must have no randomness.
The implementation is executed and admitted if its observed outputs satisfy the corpus.
witness.observer: The authoring agent and later callers of a flow using the implementation.

open_points.subject: determinism of admission for time- or chance-dependent implementations
open_points.text: K-05 says “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus,” but changed K-02 permits undetected time- or chance-dependent code to be “judged by its outputs,” and M08 records the first verdict permanently for that implementation and corpus digest.
open_points.question: For an implementation whose trial outputs can vary with time or chance, what fact makes its admission verdict deterministic for a fixed implementation and corpus?
options: Such implementations cannot receive an admission verdict
The first observed admission executions determine and permanently cache either verdict, even though another first execution could have produced the opposite verdict
Admission has an unstated mechanism that makes executions deterministic
open_points.default_guess: The first observed executions determine and permanently cache the verdict.

witness.initial: The corpus expects output 0, and an implementation can produce either 0 or 1 from an undetected source of chance; no verdict exists yet for the pair.
events: An agent submits the implementation for admission.
outcomes: The pair receives a permanently reused admitted verdict because the observed trial produced 0.
The same pair receives a permanently reused refused verdict because the observed trial produced 1.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and anyone later trying to activate or run that implementation.
